metadata.title: Reflections on the Development of the IEA Civic and Citizenship Education Studies

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This chapter is a conceptual and methodological reflection on the development of IEA civic and citizenship education studies (CIVED 1999, ICCS 2009, ICCS 2016, and upcoming ICCS 2022). It describes assessment design choices such as rotated booklets, linking items, and scaling approaches (IRT and plausible values/WLE), but it does not report an empirical student-level analysis with an analytic sample. Because no microdata model is estimated here, the chapter does not specify whether analysts should apply student/sampling weights or replicate weights in secondary analyses. For users of ICCS/CIVED microdata, the appropriate approach is to follow the official IEA scaling and analysis guidance for complex survey design and PV/WLE estimation, but those operational details are not provided in this chapter.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because this chapter does not estimate any student-level predictive or outcome models; it instead discusses how ICCS/CIVED instruments and scaling methods evolved over time (e.g., rotated booklets, IRT scaling, and the use of plausible values/WLE in ICCS). Missing-data handling is not reported because no empirical dataset is analyzed in this chapter; therefore, there is no missingness strategy to document for an estimation procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined because the chapter is not an empirical study; it reviews and compares assessment design, instrument content, scaling, and methodological changes across CIVED 1999, ICCS 2009, and ICCS 2016.

data.outcome_summary: This chapter provides a methodological reflection on how the IEA civic and citizenship education studies were designed and how they changed across cycles. It contrasts CIVED 1999 with ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016, focusing on content expansion (e.g., stronger emphasis on participation and reasoning/applying), design changes (e.g., rotated booklets for broader cognitive coverage and fatigue control), and method changes (e.g., introduction of open-ended items and coding, and the move to plausible value methodology in ICCS). It also explains how regional modules were incorporated and how questionnaire formats and classifications evolved, which affects comparability across time. The chapter further outlines expected challenges for ICCS 2022, including optional computer-based delivery and procedures to review mode effects. No student-level predictive modeling is conducted, so no ML performance metrics or causal effects are reported.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided text is a book chapter focused on assessment development, comparability, and methodological design decisions rather than on an empirical ML analysis. As a result, there is no reported analytic sample size, no country-level sample table, no model estimation, and no ML algorithm evaluation. The chapter also does not specify PV or missing-data handling for an estimation procedure because it does not run such an analysis; it only describes that ICCS uses plausible value methodology in its scaling framework.
